themes_detail.label: Street Condition Deterioration Spike
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints exploded to 213 THIS WEEK, a 625% spike versus the 8-week average of 29.4 weekly complaints (z-score: 14.49), suggesting a rapid, district-wide pavement or infrastructure failure requiring immediate investigation into root cause.
evidence: 213 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 29.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (625% increase)
Z-score of 14.49 indicates statistically extreme deviation
610 DOB permits filed in last 90 days (417 alterations) suggests active construction that may be contributing
reporting_angles: Map the 213 complaints to identify which corridors or neighborhoods in Sunnyside/Woodside are most affected; interview residents on specific hazards (potholes, cracked sidewalks, etc.)
Contact Department of Transportation to determine if recent weather, construction, or maintenance backlogs are driving the spike; obtain internal assessment data

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Crisis Emerges
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints spiked 3900% in the last 2 weeks (5 complaints vs. 0.1 weekly average, z-score: 14.74), suggesting a sudden outbreak of unauthorized signage, graffiti, or advertisements across the district.
evidence: 5 illegal posting complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average (3900% spike)
Z-score of 14.74 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Concurrent spike in street sweeping complaints (6 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 avg, up 2300%) suggests visual blight accumulation
reporting_angles: Photograph and document specific illegal posting locations; interview residents on whether this is new or worsening
Obtain NYPD/DoSanitation records to determine if a specific entity (political campaign, contractor, vendor) is behind the posting wave

themes_detail.label: Site Safety & Construction Hazards
themes_detail.summary: Building/site safety complaints surged THIS WEEK to 3 complaints versus a 0.1 weekly average (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69), while Building/Use violations rose 357% last week (12 vs. 2.6 average), indicating emerging construction site hazards or unsafe building conditions.
evidence: 3 BEST/Site Safety complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 average (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69)
12 Building/Use complaints last week vs. 2.6 weekly average (357% increase, z-score: 5.21)
103 new building permits and 417 alteration permits filed in last 90 days; likely active construction creating safety exposures
reporting_angles: Identify which active construction sites (per DOB permit data) have generated complaints; inspect for OSHA/building code violations
Interview FDNY and DOB inspectors on whether they are seeing a pattern of unsafe conditions; determine if contractor accountability is lacking

themes_detail.label: Rodent & Animal Sanitation Spike
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints surged 196% two weeks ago (10 vs. 3.4 weekly average, z-score: 4.2), and unsanitary animal private property complaints hit 3 THIS WEEK versus 0.2 average (1100% spike, z-score: 6.35), signaling an emerging pest control and animal waste crisis.
evidence: 3 unsanitary animal private property complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 average (1100% spike, z-score: 6.35)
10 rodent complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 3.4 weekly average (196% increase, z-score: 4.2)
Concurrent illegal posting/street sweeping spike suggests overall environmental conditions deteriorating; may indicate inadequate waste management
reporting_angles: Identify which neighborhoods or blocks are reporting animal and rodent complaints; inspect for exposed trash, inadequate fencing, or animal hoarding
Contact NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene to determine if Sunnyside/Woodside is seeing higher pest infestation rates; ask if they have initiated targeted outreach

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement & Street Enforcement
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints jumped 433% last week (4 vs. 0.8 weekly average, z-score: 3.92), suggesting either a surge in unlicensed street vending or a recent city enforcement initiative creating friction with vendors and residents.
evidence: 4 vendor enforcement complaints last week vs. 0.8 weekly average (433% increase, z-score: 3.92)
Coincides with illegal posting spike, suggesting broader street disorder or enforcement push
No recent community board or constituent service data available to contextualize complaint driver
reporting_angles: Interview street vendors and business owners to determine if recent enforcement actions or new regulations are sparking complaints
Obtain NYPD and Department of Consumer Affairs records to assess whether vendor-related activity or enforcement intensity has changed
